_comment: The three deportations from Judah to Babylon (597, 586, 582 BCE). Dotted lines, slightly offset so all three are visible. Sources: 2 Kings 24-25, Jeremiah 52:28-30, Babylonian Chronicle.

popup.bible: 'He carried into exile all Jerusalem: all the officials and all the warriors, ten thousand captives' (2 Kgs 24:14).
popup.archaeology: The Babylonian Chronicle confirms the capture; the Jehoiachin ration tablets show the exiled king living at court, receiving oil.

popup.bible: 'The rest of the people who were left in the city he carried into exile... but left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and tillers of the soil' (2 Kgs 25:11-12).
popup.archaeology: The city's elite are taken; the poor remain to farm. This is standard Neo-Babylonian policy: remove the leaders, keep the labor.
popup.source: 2 Kings 25; Lipschits, The Fall and Rise of Jerusalem

popup.bible: 'In the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar... he carried away captive of the Jews 745 persons' (Jer 52:30).
popup.archaeology: A punitive deportation after the assassination of Gedaliah, the Babylonian-appointed governor — the last gasp of the old order.
